correctness_confidence.basis: All three main theorems, algebraic identities, asymptotic and non-asymptotic bounds, Table 2 values, and Figure 2/3 numerical extrema were independently verified directly from the manuscript PDF. No genuine mathematical or proof gaps were found; one minor notational slip in Theorem 3(c) (writing 1/(2m_6) instead of 1/(2(m_6-1)) when bounding |Delta m_i| < 1) does not affect validity because |Delta m_i| < 0.61 and both bounds sit well below 1.14e-5.

novelty.basis: While building directly on the framework and cited Diophantine inputs of Leshem and Sayag (arXiv:2611.34736v1), the paper establishes exact minimax optimality of (ln 5)^(1/4) for the Remond-vs-diagonal trade-off, proves a clean universal Stirling-centered falling-factorial sandwich eliminating O(K^2) bias, and collapses the Lind-Singmaster counting error to an exact {0,1} law via Lucas identities and Q(sqrt(5)) simplification.

reproducibility.basis: Analytic proofs and Table 2 checkpoints (i=1..5) are self-contained and reproducible from the PDF, and SHA-256 certificate digests are tabulated in Table 3. However, the manuscript does not print the explicit 8 subinterval endpoints of C03 or the 12 handoff endpoints [l_D, l'_D] of C04 (though independent estimation confirms such contiguous intervals exist with ample margin), and the Lean 4 and Python verification artifacts reside externally.

rigor.basis: Uniform all-x >= 3, all k >= 2 / n >= 2k, and all x >= 3003 bounds are proved with explicit constants and careful regime splitting, complemented by Robbins-Stirling two-sided bounds and Lagrange remainder control for i >= 6.

significance.basis: Sharpens all three quantitative pillars of recent density estimates for repeated entries in Pascal's triangle to their natural analytic or minimax limits (43.5%-43.7% exponent reduction in A_2(x), halved effective Bombieri-Pila exponent for A_2(x), bias-free A_1(x) expansion, and sharp {0,1} Lind-Singmaster law), though it does not advance Singmaster's conjecture itself beyond cited Diophantine results.

summary: The manuscript sharpens the three main quantitative results of Leshem and Sayag (arXiv:2611.34736v1) on repeated entries in Pascal's triangle. Theorem 1 lowers the global upper bound exponent constant for A_H(x) <= A_2(x) from 2 to 113/100 uniformly for all x >= 3 and asymptotically to (ln 5)^(1/4) approx 1.1263, proves exact minimax optimality of (ln 5)^(1/4) for the Remond-versus-diagonal trade-off U_Rem(x; D), and improves the effective Bombieri-Pila exponents to 1/12 + eps (H=2) and 1/15 + eps (H=3) by excluding the four completely solved collision pairs. Theorem 2 establishes a universal Stirling-centered falling-factorial sandwich around m = n - (k-1)/2 for all k >= 2 and n >= 2k, yielding a zero-unknown-constant diagonal counting bracket and removing the -3/4(K-1)(K+2) systematic bias from the truncated expansion of A_1(x). Theorem 3 proves exact Lucas identities for the Lind-Singmaster family, collapses the entropy constant c to (varphi^4 / sqrt(5)) ln varphi, derives a three-term Robbins-Stirling expansion, and sharpens the counting error to {0, 1} for all x >= 3003 with 100% asymptotic density of exact floor equality in log log x.
strengths: Exact minimax theorem (Theorem 1(b)) proving (ln 5)^(1/4) is the unimprovable limit of the Remond-versus-diagonal upper bound functional, paired with a uniform all-x >= 3 bound within 0.33% of that limit.

Clean, elementary, and completely self-contained proof of the universal centered falling-factorial sandwich (Theorem 2(a)) and resulting bias-free K-diagonal union approximation (Theorem 2(b)-(c)) with sharp remainder R_K(x).

Elegant Q(sqrt(5)) collapse of c and exact Lucas representations in Theorem 3(a)-(b), leading to an explicit {0,1} discrepancy law for all x >= 3003 with rigorously certified bounds for i >= 6 and super-exponentially decaying failure measure mu_i ~ i / (2c varphi^(4i)).
High internal numerical consistency across text, Tables 1-2, and Figures 1-3 (e.g., exact K=4 extrema at x=5995 and Table 2 Robbins-Stirling residuals).
weaknesses: Theorem 1(a) and 1(c) rely directly on the framework and cited Diophantine bounds of Leshem and Sayag [1] (Remond's genus >= 2 bound and Bombieri-Pila Proposition 3.2) rather than introducing new Diophantine geometry.
The explicit interval endpoints for the 8 subintervals in Regime II (Certificate C03) and the 12 handoff intervals [l_D, l'_D] in Regime III (Certificate C04) are not tabulated in the PDF itself.
Independent auditing strictly from the PDF cannot verify the external Lean 4 formalization, Python zero-float verifier, or SHA-256 certificate payloads beyond the summaries in Section 5 and Table 3.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact minimax optimality of (ln 5)^(1/4) for the Remond-versus-diagonal trade-off functional U_Rem(x; D) (Theorem 1(b)).
Universal Stirling-centered falling-factorial sandwich max(m^k(1 - k(k^2-1)/(24m^2)), (m - 3(k^2-1)/(64m))^k) <= (n)_k < m^k and bias-free A_1(x) expansion (Theorem 2).

Exact Lucas identities 5n_i = L_{4i+5}-1, 5k_i = L_{4i+3}-4, 5m_i = L_{4i+4}+3, Q(sqrt(5)) collapse c = (varphi^4/sqrt(5)) ln varphi, and exact {0,1} Lind-Singmaster counting law for all x >= 3003 (Theorem 3).
potential_errors: Minor expositional slip in the proof of Theorem 3(c) (p. 8): writing 1/(2m_6) instead of 1/(2(m_6-1)) when bounding |Delta m_i| < 1; the stated bound < 1.14e-5 remains strictly true since |Delta m_i| < 0.61.
